subject: humanities
passage: The Warli, a community living in the hills north of Mumbai, in western India, have long decorated the mud walls of their homes with paintings. The painters use only a white paste made from rice, applied with a chewed bamboo stick, on a background of reddish-brown earth. Their pictures are built from a few simple shapes: circles, triangles, and squares. A circle and two triangles joined at the tips become a dancing figure, and rows of such figures become a wedding or a harvest.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To explain how the rice paste used in Warli painting is prepared
choices.B: To compare Warli painting with other art traditions of India
choices.C: To describe the materials and basic shapes used in Warli painting
choices.D: To argue that simple shapes make better art than detailed ones

explanation.why: After introducing the Warli, the text describes what they paint with (rice paste, a bamboo stick, an earth background) and what they paint from (circles, triangles, squares) and shows how those shapes combine into figures and scenes. The purpose is to describe the materials and shapes of the art.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says the paste is made from rice but never explains how it is prepared.
explanation.B: Incorrect. No other art tradition is mentioned, so there is no comparison.
explanation.C: Correct. The text describes the paste, the stick, the earth background, and the three shapes from which Warli pictures are built.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text describes the Warli's use of simple shapes without claiming that such art is better than any other kind.
